sources.title: CTT Collaborators (2010) — Efficacy of LDL-lowering and vascular events
sources.snippet: Each 1 mmol/L reduction in LDL reduces major vascular events by ~22%

sources.title: Ference et al. (2017) — LDL and cardiovascular risk: Mendelian randomization
sources.snippet: Genetically-instrumented LDL-lowering: OR 0.54 per mmol/L for CHD

beta_lipid_cv.reasoning: Strong causal evidence from Mendelian randomization and CTT meta-analysis: LDL is a direct driver of atherosclerosis

sources.title: Ettehad et al. (2016) — Blood pressure lowering and CV risk
sources.snippet: 10 mmHg SBP reduction: 20% lower major CV events, 17% lower CHD

sources.title: SPRINT Research Group (2015) — Intensive vs standard BP targets
sources.snippet: Intensive BP control (SBP <120) reduced CV events by 25% vs standard (<140)

beta_pressure_cv.reasoning: Well-established dose-response: every 10 mmHg SBP reduction yields ~20% CV risk reduction

sources.title: UKPDS 35 (2000) — HbA1c and complications in T2DM
sources.snippet: Each 1% reduction in HbA1c: 14% reduction in MI, 21% reduction in diabetes deaths

sources.title: Holman et al. (2008) — UKPDS 10-year post-trial monitoring
sources.snippet: Legacy effect: early intensive glycemic control continued to reduce MI risk 10 years later

beta_glycemic_cv.reasoning: Negative effect: better glycemic control (higher construct value) reduces CV risk. UKPDS established the dose-response.

sources.title: Ridker et al. (2008) — CRP, LDL, and cardiovascular events (JUPITER)
sources.snippet: Rosuvastatin reduced LDL by 50% and hs-CRP by 37%, with 44% reduction in CV events

sources.title: Libby et al. (2011) — Inflammation in atherosclerosis pathogenesis
sources.snippet: Oxidized LDL drives monocyte recruitment and foam cell formation; CRP tracks atherogenic inflammatory burden

beta_lipid_inflammation.reasoning: Strong positive effect: atherogenic lipids drive vascular inflammation through oxidized LDL infiltration and foam cell formation. JUPITER showed statins reduce both LDL and CRP.

sources.title: Ridker et al. (2017) — CANTOS: Anti-inflammatory therapy and CV outcomes
sources.snippet: Canakinumab (anti-IL-1β) reduced hs-CRP by 39% and major CV events by 15%, without lowering LDL

sources.title: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration (2010) — CRP and CV disease
sources.snippet: Log-linear association: each SD increase in log CRP associated with RR 1.37 for CHD

beta_inflammation_cv.reasoning: CANTOS proved causality: targeting inflammation directly (without lipid changes) reduces CV events. CRP is independently predictive of CV risk.

sources.title: CARDS Trial (2004) — Atorvastatin in T2DM
sources.snippet: Atorvastatin 10mg in T2DM: 37% reduction in acute coronary events

beta_adherence_lipid.reasoning: Statin adherence directly reduces LDL burden; strong negative effect.

sources.title: HOPE Trial (2000) — Ramipril and CV events
sources.snippet: Ramipril reduced CV death, MI, stroke by 22% in high-risk patients

beta_adherence_pressure.reasoning: ACE-inhibitor adherence reduces arterial pressure; ramipril has proven CV benefit beyond BP lowering.

sources.title: Mora et al. (2019) — LDL autocorrelation in statin-treated patients
sources.snippet: Month-to-month LDL variability shows moderate autocorrelation (rho ~0.7) in stable patients on statin therapy

rho_lipid.reasoning: LDL is highly persistent month-to-month (slow metabolic turnover)

sources.title: Muntner et al. (2015) — Visit-to-visit BP variability
sources.snippet: Visit-to-visit SBP variability shows high persistence (ICC ~0.65) in treated hypertensives

rho_pressure.reasoning: Blood pressure moderately autocorrelated; more variable than lipids

sources.title: Bangalore et al. (2015) — LDL-C variability and cardiovascular outcomes
sources.snippet: Residual LDL variability (SD ~0.3-0.5 mmol/L) after accounting for treatment effects in statin trials

sigma_lipid.reasoning: Weakly informative prior on lipid residual SD

sources.title: Rothwell et al. (2010) — BP variability and stroke risk
sources.snippet: Residual within-patient SBP variability ~5-10 mmHg after detrending, independent of mean BP level

sigma_pressure.reasoning: Weakly informative prior on BP residual SD (mmHg scale)

sources.title: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration (2010) — CRP stability
sources.snippet: Within-person CRP shows moderate temporal stability (ICC ~0.6) over months

rho_inflammation.reasoning: CRP has moderate month-to-month persistence; Beta(4,2) centers at 0.67 reflecting this autocorrelation.

sources.title: Mora et al. (2014) — Lipid biomarker factor structure
sources.snippet: Triglycerides load 0.6–0.9 on a common atherogenic lipid factor alongside LDL in CFA models

lambda_triglycerides_lipid_burden.reasoning: Triglycerides co-load with LDL on atherogenic lipid burden; weakly informative HalfNormal allows data to determine scale.

sources.title: Nordestgaard & Varbo (2014) — Triglycerides and cardiovascular disease
sources.snippet: HDL inversely associated with atherogenic lipid burden; factor loadings typically 0.4–0.8 in lipid CFA

lambda_hdl_cholesterol_lipid_burden.reasoning: HDL reflects lipid burden inversely; constraint is positive here since the construct represents net atherogenic load and HDL measurement direction is handled in the link function.

sources.title: Fibrinogen Studies Collaboration (2005) — Plasma fibrinogen and CV disease
sources.snippet: Fibrinogen and CRP show moderate correlation (r ≈ 0.4–0.5) as co-indicators of systemic inflammation

lambda_fibrinogen_vascular_inflammation.reasoning: Fibrinogen is an acute-phase reactant loading on the same vascular inflammation factor as CRP; HalfNormal(1) is weakly informative.

sources.title: DCCT/EDIC Research Group (2005) — HbA1c and glucose as glycemic markers
sources.snippet: Fasting glucose and HbA1c correlate r ≈ 0.7 as co-indicators of glycemic regulation

lambda_fasting_glucose_glycemic_control.reasoning: Fasting glucose and HbA1c both reflect underlying glycemic control; weakly informative prior lets the data determine the relative scaling.

sources.title: Franklin et al. (2009) — Systolic vs diastolic BP components
sources.snippet: SBP and DBP correlate r ≈ 0.7 and load on a common arterial pressure factor

lambda_diastolic_bp_arterial_pressure.reasoning: Diastolic BP co-loads with systolic BP on an arterial pressure factor; factor loading typically near 0.7–0.9.

sources.title: Palatini & Julius (2004) — Heart rate and cardiovascular risk
sources.snippet: Resting heart rate reflects sympathetic tone and loads modestly on hemodynamic factors (λ ≈ 0.3–0.5)

lambda_resting_heart_rate_arterial_press.reasoning: Heart rate is a weaker indicator of arterial pressure than SBP/DBP, reflecting autonomic rather than purely vascular tone; prior allows both weak and strong loadings.

sources.title: Osterberg & Blaschke (2005) — Adherence to medication
sources.snippet: Appointment attendance and prescription renewal are correlated behavioral markers of treatment engagement (r ≈ 0.5–0.7)

lambda_appointment_attendance_medication.reasoning: Appointment attendance and prescription renewals co-load on a latent medication adherence factor; weakly informative prior.

sources.snippet: Within-person biological variability of LDL cholesterol: CV ~8–10%

sigma_ldl_cholesterol.reasoning: Observation noise for LDL cholesterol reflects biological variation and lab assay imprecision (CV ~9%).

sources.title: Marcovina et al. (1994) — Biological variability of lipids
sources.snippet: Within-person CV for triglycerides is 20–25%, higher than other lipids

sigma_triglycerides.reasoning: Triglycerides have higher measurement noise than other lipids due to fasting variation and diurnal effects.

sources.title: Smith et al. (1993) — Biological variability of HDL
sources.snippet: Within-person biological variability of HDL cholesterol: CV ~7–8%

sigma_hdl_cholesterol.reasoning: HDL has moderate measurement noise from biological variation and assay imprecision.

sources.title: Macy et al. (1997) — Variability of CRP
sources.snippet: Within-person CV for hs-CRP is 30–50% reflecting acute-phase fluctuations

sigma_crp.reasoning: CRP has high within-person variability due to acute inflammatory triggers; weakly informative HalfNormal allows flexible noise estimation.

sources.title: Fibrinogen Studies Collaboration (2005)
sources.snippet: Within-person CV for fibrinogen ~10–15%

sigma_fibrinogen.reasoning: Fibrinogen measurement noise from biological variation and assay imprecision.

sources.title: Rohlfing et al. (2002) — Biological variation of HbA1c
sources.snippet: Within-person CV for HbA1c is ~3–4% in stable patients

sigma_hba1c.reasoning: HbA1c is a stable 3-month average with low measurement noise; tighter prior reflects this.

sources.title: Mooy et al. (1996) — Intra-individual variation of fasting glucose

sigma_resting_heart_rate.reasoning: Resting heart rate varies with anxiety, caffeine, activity level at time of measurement.
